# Browser tests

Playwright tests run against the separate test backend (Docker project `moneo-qa`, `.env.qa`) and this checkout's app on http://localhost:3100. The config starts the app with `npm run qa:server` (or a production build with `E2E_PRODUCTION_BUILD=1`) unless it is already running.

## Setup

1. Create the test backend once (and after pulling new migrations): `npm run setup -- --qa`.
2. Create the QA user and save its session: `npm run qa:auth`. Its login is stored in `.env.qa` as `E2E_USER_EMAIL`/`E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, and its session in `e2e/.auth.json` (or set `E2E_STORAGE_STATE`).
3. Before a full run, empty its workspace: `npm run qa:reset`.

The whole test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` and step 1 start it fresh. The owner's `moneo` project is never touched.

Tests never use the owner's workspace. Every spec runs with the saved QA session and an `x-moneo-test` header; with that header the app refuses a request that has no valid session instead of signing the owner in (`proxy.ts`). Before any spec runs, `e2e/global-setup.ts` checks that the server under test does this, so an older or foreign server on the port stops the run.

## Running

```sh
npm run test:e2e -- --workers=1
```

Use one worker: several specs change the same QA workspace and its preferences. The QA server builds into `.next-qa`, so it can run beside `npm run dev`.

## Kinds of specs

- `*.smoke.spec.ts` and `*.mocked.spec.ts` stub or skip the backend. Against a configured backend they still need the QA session, like every spec.
- `*.gated.spec.ts` need the backend. Most use the QA session; others create disposable users with the service key, sign them in by session cookie, and remove them in `finally`. If interrupted, their IDs are left in ignored `.qa/` files for cleanup.
- `*.provider.spec.ts` call the real AI model, so they cost money. They run only with `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; `npm run test:e2e` leaves them out.
- `review-runtime.config.ts` and `review-investigation.config.ts` run the real Workflow engine against local synthetic database and model servers (ports 3040/3041), including a server restart mid-review: `npx playwright test --config e2e/review-runtime.config.ts`.

## Nightly

`npm run qa:nightly -- --install` schedules the whole suite for 03:00 every day (a Windows scheduled task that starts as soon as possible if the PC was off). It runs every spec twice on a production build of `origin/main`, in its own worktree in `~/.moneo/nightly`, and keeps one GitHub issue, "Nightly browser suite is failing", up to date. A night with Docker off or port 3100 busy is skipped quietly; the log is `~/.moneo/nightly.log`.

A skipped spec is not a pass: it means a prerequisite (backend, QA session, service key) is missing.

## Scalable

`scalable-trading.provider.spec.ts` drives chat against a local stand-in for Scalable's MCP server (`e2e/mocks/scalable-mcp.mjs`, made-up data) with the real AI model. Start `npm run qa:server` with `SCALABLE_MCP_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:3043` (and the AI key in `.env.qa`) and run the spec with the same variable and `E2E_REAL_AI=1`; the spec starts the stand-in, adds a Scalable connection to the QA workspace and removes it afterwards. It checks that an order is previewed on a card and sent only when the card is tapped, once, and that read-only access is told it can't trade.

content.text:
On a phone, Moneo now looks and behaves like a native app, and the desktop layout is unchanged. The changes are in PR https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/198 (not merged).

![Light mode on iPhone 14: scrolled header, More sheet, search, Home, Ask](C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-efa2dc73-1ac8c7c673fc3cfd\.qa\mobile\i-light.png)
![Dark mode](C:\Users\mgsuk\.t3\worktrees\Moneo\t3-efa2dc73-1ac8c7c673fc3cfd\.qa\mobile\i-dark.png)

**What changed on phones:**
- **Header:** each page starts with its big title. Once you scroll past it, the title moves into a slim see-through bar with search and notifications, like iOS apps do. Sub-pages (Ledger / Organization / …) are a segmented control.
- **Tab bar:** Home · Transactions · **Ask** (in the middle) · Plan · More. Ask opens the chat full screen, straight away. More is a sheet with everything else, including Accounts, Wealth and Settings.
- **Chat:** the app's header and tab bar are hidden. The chat has its own bar with back, title, past conversations, new chat, deep review and call. The message box sits at the bottom, clear of the iPhone notch and home bar.
- **Page fixes:**
  - Settings and Import no longer scroll sideways on small phones, and the Wealth form fits.
  - Rows of filter chips scroll in one line instead of wrapping.
  - Form fields go full width.
  - Save bars stay above the tab bar.
  - Text fields no longer make iOS zoom in when you tap them.

**How I checked it:**
- I screenshotted every page on iPhone 14 in light and dark mode.
- I checked for sideways scrolling on a 360px-wide Android phone (Galaxy S8), iPhone SE and iPad Mini.
- Unit tests, lint, typecheck and the production build pass, and so do the four browser test files that cover these screens.
- All of this ran against the test backend with made-up data, never your real data.

No, I hadn't checked the call before. It already filled the phone screen but looked like a web page, so I redesigned it for phones. PR https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/198 now also has before/after screenshots for every screen.

**The call on phones now:**
- No title bar. "Moneo" is in large type at the top, with the call timer (0:42) underneath, like a phone call.
- A big orb sits in the middle and shows whether Moneo is listening, thinking, talking or you're muted.
- Three round buttons at the bottom: **Mute · Keypad · End**. The text box only appears when you tap Keypad.
- The queries you ask during the call are listed under the orb with done, failed or running icons. Once the list appears, the orb shrinks so the queries stay on screen.

The desktop call screen is unchanged. Unit tests and lint pass. One test run failed only because it ran alongside the dev server; with the server stopped, all 1551 tests passed.

**What I couldn't check:** a real live call. The test setup uses a fake AI key, so a real call goes straight to "Call dropped". I showed each call state with made-up data in a temporary page that I've since deleted. Please try one real call on your iPhone.

**About the "before" pictures:** I didn't build the old version again. They're the screenshots I took at the start, before I loaded test data, so they show fewer transactions than the "after" ones. The PR images are on a separate branch, `pr-198-screenshots`, which only holds those pictures; delete it after merging if you like.
